To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
deep convolutional neural network (CNN) based classification is a promising approach for large scale LULC classification, and that the OpenStreetMap is a suitable source for training data.

deep learning methods for image recognition are also well suited to solve LULC classification problems and that the use of crowdsourced data for training can reduce the amount of manual labor required for LULC mapping.
CNNs are well-suited for LULCC classification, that a quasi automatic method to derive labels from the OpenStreetMap can be applied to large areas, and that the resulting LULC map is of good quality.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an end-to-end approach for the automatic generation of LULC maps, which is able to provide results in a matter of hours, instead of years.
the development of a fully automated, open source method for the production of large scale LULC maps with a production time of a few weeks.
the development and evaluation of a fully automated, open source method for the generation of LULC maps with high spatial resolution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CNNs are very well suited for the classification of satellite images.

CNNs are well suited for LULC mapping, but that further research is needed to improve the quality of the labels and to investigate the influence of the spatial resolution on the classification results.
CNNs for LULC mapping can be considered a promising research direction, but further research and validation is needed to fully exploit the potential of this approach.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of deep learning methods is a promising approach to LULC mapping.
the presented method can be used for the creation of large scale LULC maps in an automated and timely fashion.
the presented CNNs are able to achieve a classification accuracy of 0.81 on a per pixel basis, while the classification of 100 x 100m image patches is achieved with 0.89.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of CNNs for LULC mapping is feasible, and that the presented method is a promising candidate for the creation of large scale LULC maps with up to near real-time production times.
CNNs can be used for the classification of large scale multispectral imagery with up to global extent and that the required labels can be derived from existing sources of geographic information.
deep CNNs are a promising alternative for large scale LULC mapping.
